 Judgment

(Dated this the 8th day of October, 2025) This appeal is filed by the appellant/4 th respondent insurer in O.P.(MV) No.570 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Pathanamthitta, challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
The respondents herein are the claimants before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimants is that on 03.05.2011 at about 8.30 pm, while the deceased was walking through the K.P road and he reached near Adoor New Private bus stand, a motorcycle bearing Registration No.KL-03-N-2249, driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit the deceased; whereby, the deceased sustained serious injuries and later succumbed to his injuries.

The legal heirs approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 37,50,000/- limited to 21,00,000/.
3.

The respondents 1 to 3 were driver, registered 2025:KER:75393 : 4 :
owner and actual owner in possession of the offending vehicle, respectively.
The 4th respondent Insurance Company filed a written statement admitting the insurance policy but denying the quantum of compensation awarded.

The Tribunal, after The Oriental Insuranceco. Ltd vs Thulasi C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18541622/
2 analysing the pleadings and materials on record, held that the accident took place on account of the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle and awarded a total compensation of 21,17,000/- as compensation under different heads with interest @9% per annum from the date of petition till realization, against the 4th respondent,
being the insurer.

sentences.text: Challenging the quantum of compensation awarded, the 4th respondent insurer has come up with this appeal.
4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/insurer and the learned Counsel for the claimants.

5. The appellant has filed this appeal challenging the quantum of compensation under the following heads:-
2025:KER:75393 : 5 :
Notional income :- On a perusal of the award it is seen that the tribunal had taken only an amount of 7,500/- as the notional income of the deceased

whereas,
following the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the income of the coolie for an accident which occurred in 2011 is fixed at 8,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that instead of adding 40% future prospects to the income fixed, the tribunal has added 50%, I find force in the argument since the deceased was a daily labourer the percentage to be added towards future prospects is 40% and not 50%.
It is true that the claimants have not filed any appeal challenging the quantum of compensation awarded.

Since the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation, and in order to meet the end of justice and to award just and reasonable compensation, I find it appropriate to enhance and refix the 2025:KER:75393 : 6 :
monthly income as 8,000/-.

Accordingly, the monthly notional income after adding 40% future prospects for assessing compensation towards loss of dependency is 11,200/- (8,000 x 40% + 3,200).
Loss of Dependency :- Since there are five legal heirs including the parents during the time of the accident, I find that deduction towards personal and living expenses is 1/4.
The deceased was aged 34 years at the time of accident, and hence the appropriate multiplier to be adopted is '16'.

Since, the monthly income after adding 40% future prospects is fixed at 11,200/-, following the judgments of the apex court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017(4) KLT 662(SC)] and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)], the compensation payable under the head loss of dependency is recalculated as thus: 16,12,800/-
(11,200 x 12 x 16 x 3/4).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017(4) KLT 662(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The tribunal has awarded an amount of 16,20,000/- under the head loss of 2025:KER:75393 : 7 :
dependency.
Hence, a deduction of 7,200/- is made under the afore head.

The Oriental Insuranceco. Ltd vs Thulasi C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18541622/
3

entities.text: Oriental Insuranceco. Ltd vs Thulasi C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Funeral expenses:-
On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has awarded an amount of 25,000/ - towards funeral expenses.
However, following the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the amount ought to have been granted by the tribunal is 15,000/-.
Accordingly, there will be a deduction of an amount of 10,000/- under the afore head.
Loss of estate:-
It is submitted by the learned standing counsel for the insurance company that the Tribunal has awarded an amount of 1,00,000/- towards loss of estate.
As per the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra) the claimants are only entitled to 15,000/- under the said head.
Accordingly, there will be a deduction of an amount of 85,000/- under the afore head.

Loss of consortium/loss of love and affection:-
2025:KER:75393 : 8 :

The learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that the tribunal has awarded an amount of 2,50,000/- towards the head loss of love and affection and 1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium whereas, the claimants were entitled only for a total amount of 2,00,000/- under both the heads together.
I find force in the said argument.

It has also been held by the Apex Court, in New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 KHC 6530], that once compensation is awarded under the head loss of consortium, no amount shall be awarded under the head loss of love and affection, as it would amount to duplication of compensation.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 KHC 6530]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I delete 2,50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head loss of love and affection and I award an additional amount of 1,00,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
6.

Though the insurer challenged the quantum of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the 2025:KER:75393 : 9 :
records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

7. Thus, the impugned award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:-

Funeral

4 9 Others 15,000 Nil Nil Nil TOTAL 37,50,000 21,17,000 (-)2,52,200 18,64,800 limited to 21,00,000

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and respondents/claimants are awarded a total compensation of 18,64,800/- (Rupees eighteen lakhs sixty four thousand eight hundred only) with interest @ 9% per annum after deducting an amount of 2,52,200/- from the impugned award from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.
The appellant/ insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The respondents/claimants shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the appellant insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.

In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said 2025:KER:75393 : 11 :
amount before the Tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the respondents at the earliest in accordance with law.

SHOBA ANNAMMA EAPEN JUDGE SRJ
